summary.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.
summary.overview: Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 3,068 crore, up 36.23% YoY, with operating profit up 25.99% to Rs 5,051 crore and NII up 12.61% to Rs 6,833 crore. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with Gross NPA at 1.81% and Net NPA at 0.51%, and slippage ratio at 0.24%. Global business grew 16.57% YoY to Rs 17.55 lakh crore, with advances up 18.64%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for advances growth of 15-16% and deposit growth of 13-14%, and raised a dollar-funding target of $4.2 billion through FCNR(B), OFCB/MTN and ECB routes by December 2026.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -111 bps YoY; NNPA -24 bps YoY

segments.name: Global business and deposits
segments.commentary: Global business Rs 17.55 lakh crore (+16.57% YoY). Global deposits Rs 9.58 lakh crore (+14.90%); domestic deposits Rs 8.25 lakh crore (+16.15%). CASA Rs 3.02 lakh crore, CASA ratio 36.68%.

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global gross advances Rs 7.98 lakh crore (+18.64% YoY); domestic advances Rs 6.74 lakh crore (+19.20%). RAM advances Rs 3.93 lakh crore (+19.75%), 58.30% of advances.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at yield of about 9.10%, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International business touched about Rs 2.56 lakh crore; around 32% of international loan book is trade finance, which management plans to reduce.

segments.name: Mutual fund subsidiary
segments.commentary: Bank of India mutual fund AUM about Rs 16,000-17,000 crore; no near-term plan for public issue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guidance unchanged at 15-16%; global deposit growth guidance unchanged at 13-14%.
Global NIM guidance for FY27 at 2.55%-2.60%, though management said NIMs are under challenge.
Cost-to-income ratio at about 46% in Q1, but guided to 48%-49% on a consistent basis during FY27.
ROA guidance of 1% and above on a consistent quarter-on-quarter basis in FY27 (Q4 FY26 1.01%, Q1 FY27 about 1%).
FCNR(B) target of $1.2 billion by 30 September 2026; OFCB/MTN target about $2 billion by 31 December 2026; ECB target about $1 billion; total dollar raising about $4.2 billion by December 2026.
capex_capacity: Opened a dedicated Strategic Business Branch in Mumbai for high-value pool buyouts, co-lending, TReDS and supply chain financing.
Centralised Video KYC centre operationalised in Mumbai for end-to-end digital account opening.
Around 22% of domestic credit book now sanctioned digitally; data lake and CRM Next linked lead flow has built business of more than Rs 18,000 crore.
ATM network rationalised: loss-making capex-model ATMs exited, reducing total ATM count by about 300.
Plans to add 19 emerging corporate credit branches' focus on Rs 25-250 crore mid-corporate advances; credit card base target of 3 lakh by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Corporate plus international pipeline about Rs 70,000 crore; total loan pipeline above Rs 1 lakh crore including RAM, digital, pool purchase, TReDS and supply chain financing.

FCNR(B) deposits: about $200 million garnered so far; three-year FCNR at 6.25%, 3-4 year at 6.30%, five-year at 6.50%; leverage product up to nine times; management cited a spread of about 50 bps on five-year deposits, with CRR/SLR not applicable.
Management declined to give current leverage spread, citing a moving target in borrowing and dollar rates; leveraged share of FCNR not quantified.
Personal loans grew only about 3% YoY after guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans.
ECLGS: about Rs 6,000 crore sanctioned, Rs 4,600 crore disbursed; expected total sanctions and disbursal of about Rs 8,000 crore by scheme end.
SMA-0 for accounts of Rs 5 crore and above fell to about Rs 4,090 crore (0.52% of standard book), from about Rs 4,700 crore at March 2026 and above Rs 7,000 crore at June 2025.
Q1 fresh slippages including incremental NPA debits about Rs 1,800 crore vs Rs 2,100 crore in Q1 FY26; sectors under watch include chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas importers/exporters.
PSL income about Rs 277 crore in Q1; management said further PSL income possible in Q2 and Q3 but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Is stress visible in MSME and small loan accounts from the West Asia crisis, and what is the ECLGS position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMA and slippages show no major stress; ECLGS sanctions of about Rs 6,000 crore with Rs 4,600 crore disbursed, expected to reach about Rs 8,000 crore. Certain sectors are being monitored closely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB plan and how does the leverage product work?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) target is $1.2 billion by 30 September; OFCB/MTN about $2 billion by 31 December; ECB about $1 billion (about $500 million already approved in principle). Leverage product is up to nine times, with three-year FCNR at 6.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at about 9.10% yield, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore; three-notice, 90-day auction SOP applied.

qa_highlights.question: Why did personal loans grow only 3%, and what is the credit card plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans, shifting to salaried and service-sector borrowers with NACH. Credit card base target is 3 lakh by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CASA and retail term deposit ratios fall while cost of deposits dropped 15 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly 3% fall in CASA and retail term deposit share, as bulk deposits above Rs 3 crore were used to fund credit growth; cost of deposits was reduced via Rs 3-25 crore FD campaign and mix changes.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM and CIR hold, and how will yields on advances move?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is NIM 2.55%-2.60% and CIR 48%-49% for FY27. Yields on advances expected to pause falling, supported by MCLR-linked loans, mid-corporate growth and reduced low-margin trade finance.

risks_watch: Dollar-raising targets ($4.2 billion) depend on FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB windows (FCNR to 30 September; OFCB/MTN to 31 December 2026); leverage spreads are moving.
NIM under pressure from the interest rate environment and West Asia developments; guidance requires 2.55%-2.60% vs 2.52% in Q1.
CIR guidance steps up to 48%-49% from about 46% in Q1, implying higher costs ahead.
Stress in chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas-linked import/export accounts; Q1 is seasonally high for slippages per management.
Declining CASA ratio (36.68%) and retail term deposits; cost of deposits benefit depends on bulk and FCNR mix.
Treasury gains in Q1 may not repeat as yields move adversely.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, asset quality and profitability, with guidance reiterated unchanged. Cautious on NIM, the West Asia impact and sector stress, and evasive on FCNR spreads and leverage economics and on the PSU merger question.

Plans to add 19 emerging corporate credit branches focused on Rs 25-250 crore mid-corporate advances

growth.why: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and deposits at 13-14%, both unchanged; backing is a Rs 1 lakh crore+ loan pipeline (Rs 70,000 crore corporate and international) and a $4.2 billion overseas raise target by December 2026, but no new productive capacity was quantified and NIM guidance of 2.55-2.60% is under challenge.
